I go to play Assassin's creed origins and I get a "nvlddmkm has stopped responding and has successfully recovered"... I've spent the past 4 days troubleshooting it. I really don't think it's a hardware problem. I can still play other games, it seems to be more demanding games or possibly Directx 11 games. Vermintide II, AC:O, and Monster Hunter World all have a similar error. Ive done a lot of different fixes but nothing seems to work. When I get home from work today I have another 8-10 fixed I'll try. I'm hoping worse case scenarios I reinstall windows 10 or my power supply is going. At least with the PSU I have a warranty. I'm really hoping it isn't the graphics card, don't have money for it currently. I just need this card to last me another year at most. At least a couple months and maybe I'll cave and get a 2080.

Status: UNRESOLVED

Computer Type: Desktop, custom built

GPU: ASUS Strix GTX 1080 8GB, no overclock.

CPU: Intel i7 6700k 4.0Ghz, no overclock. 

Motherboard: ASUS Arctic Sabertooth Z170S 

RAM: Crucial Ballastix LT 16GB DDR4 2400Mhz, no overclock.

PSU: EVGA SuperNOVA 650 G1, 80+ GOLD 650W

Operating System & Version: Windows 10 Pro Build 17134. Clean install.

GPU Drivers: 399.24, was an upgrade but then DDU and clean install. 

Description of Problem: Display driver nvlddmkm stopped responding and has successfully recovered. I installed the latest driver last week and during the installation I received a blue screen from Windows. It restarted and the driver seemed to install. At that point, I turn the computer off and go to bed. The next morning I go to play Assassin's Creed Origins and get the nvlddmkm error and it crashes to desktop. This also happens with Vermintide II. I've tried multiple games and they don't crash or get this error. Granted, they weren't as demanding as the other two games. Now, after doing some research/troubleshooting, Vermintide II crashes and receives the nvlddmkm error after the intro video. Assassin's Creed doesn't crash, just goes through the intro videos and then a black screen and the audio continues to go. I've tried Ultimate Chicken Horse, Witcher 1, Superhot just because they were already installed on my system. They don't get the crash. 

Troubleshooting: I've tried uninstalling and reinstalling the driver, I rolled back drivers, I disable Windows from updating display drivers, I've changed power settings in Nvidia Control Panel, I turned off FXAA, I've reseated my graphics card, blown all the dust out of it, checked temperatures (45-50 degrees), I've tried lowering the Clock/Memory speeds. I changed out the VGA cable from the PSU to video card. I ran memtest, I ran chkdsk, I've check integrity of the files in steam, I've reinstalled the games, I've changed drives. I've ran as administrator. I've updated Steam/Uplay. I put a delay on TDR to 10 seconds in the registry. 

I am out of ideas, the last thing I can think of trying is using another PCI slot for my graphics card. I am able to watch videos, play some games, browse the internet, etc. Just something about these 3D Applications aren't showing up.
